gaps.sentence: Unless you ___ the form by Friday, your application will not be considered.
gaps.hint: unless means if not, present simple
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if not' and, like if, takes the present simple: submit.

gaps.sentence: I will tell her the news when I ___ her at the party.
gaps.hint: when clauses take present for future
gaps.explanation: Time clauses with future meaning use the present simple, not 'will': see.

gaps.sentence: I would never have found the house if you ___ me the postcode.
gaps.explanation: The unreal past condition takes the past perfect: had not sent.

gaps.sentence: You ___ the truth if you had asked me directly.
gaps.hint: a passive result in the third conditional
gaps.explanation: The third-conditional result clause can be passive: would have been told.

gaps.sentence: If I ___ a million euros, I would travel the world for a year.
gaps.explanation: Second conditionals use the past simple after 'if' for unreal presents: won.

gaps.sentence: If you had watered the plants, they ___.
gaps.hint: negative unreal past result with would
gaps.explanation: The unreal past result takes 'would not have' plus the past participle: would not have died.

gaps.sentence: He wishes he ___ harder at school when he had the chance.
gaps.hint: past regret, wish plus past perfect
gaps.explanation: Regret about past behavior takes the past perfect after 'wish': had worked.

gaps.sentence: If you mix blue and yellow, you always ___ green.
gaps.explanation: The adverb 'always' signals a timeless result, so the present simple fits: get.
